satori.help.title: Mahjong rules
satori.help.no_results: No matching yaku. Try another word or clear the search.
satori.help.live: Play continues · Esc returns to table
satori.help.scroll: Scroll with the wheel or arrow keys. Page Up / Down and Home / End also work.
satori.help.basics.win.title: Complete shape + yaku + legal win
satori.help.basics.win.body: A yaku is a qualifying condition, such as Riichi or All Simples. You need a complete hand and at least one yaku. Tsumo wins on your own draw; ron wins on another player's discard. Furiten blocks ron.
satori.help.basics.dora.title: Dora adds value, not a yaku
satori.help.basics.dora.body: Dora and red fives add han only after a yaku is present. Four groups and a pair with dora alone cannot win.
satori.help.basics.furiten.title: Furiten blocks ron, not tsumo
satori.help.basics.furiten.body: If any tile completing your current shape is in your own discards, you cannot ron on any wait. Passing a ron also causes furiten. See Riichi.
satori.help.basics.shape.title: The usual shape: four groups and a pair
satori.help.basics.shape.body: A sequence is three consecutive numbers in one suit; a triplet is three identical tiles. A pair is two identical tiles. Four identical tiles count as a group only as a declared kan. Seven Pairs and Thirteen Orphans are exceptions.
satori.help.basics.routes.title: Common hand plans
satori.help.basics.routes.body: Stay closed and declare riichi when ready; use only numbers 2–8 for All Simples; or collect a triplet of dragons, your seat wind or the round wind. Before calling, check which yaku will remain.
satori.help.basics.example.title: A complete hand with a yaku
satori.help.basics.example.body: 234 characters, 345 dots, 678 bamboo, three white dragons and a pair of East: four groups and a pair. White dragons provide one han, open or closed. Replacing that triplet with an ordinary sequence means you need another yaku.
satori.help.play.tiles.title: Tiles: three suits and seven honors
satori.help.play.tiles.body: Characters, dots and bamboo each run from 1 to 9. Honors are East, South, West, North, white, green and red dragons. Four copies of each make 136 tiles. A red five is a five plus one dora. Terminals are 1 and 9; honors cannot form sequences.
satori.help.play.turn.title: Your turn: draw, then discard
satori.help.play.turn.body: Normally you hold 13 tiles; draw to 14 and discard one. The dealer starts with an extra tile and discards first. Tenpai means one tile short of a complete hand. Declared groups remain part of the hand.
satori.help.play.seats.title: Seat winds, round wind and turn order
satori.help.play.seats.body: Seats are East, South, West and North; East is the dealer. Turns run East → South → West → North. The player before you is on your left. Seat winds rotate with the dealer; the round wind changes between East and South rounds.
satori.help.play.chi.title: Chi: a sequence from the player on your left
satori.help.play.chi.body: Combine two tiles with the left player's discard to make a same-suit sequence, expose it, then discard. You cannot chi from the other seats or chi honors. Immediate swap-calling is restricted at this table.
satori.help.play.pon.title: Pon: a triplet from any player
satori.help.play.pon.body: With a pair, call any player's matching discard, expose the triplet and discard. Pon changes turn order and opens the hand. You cannot immediately discard the same tile you just called.
satori.help.play.kan.title: Kan: four identical tiles, then a replacement draw
satori.help.play.kan.body: Open kan uses three tiles plus a discard. Added kan extends an exposed pon. Concealed kan uses four tiles in your hand. A kan gets a replacement draw and another dora indicator. It is still one group in the winning shape.
satori.help.play.closed.title: Closed hands and open hands
satori.help.play.closed.body: A concealed kan and winning by ron preserve a closed hand. Chi, pon and open or added kan open it. Riichi and Pinfu then become unavailable; some other yaku lose one han. Calling a tile is not itself a yaku.
satori.help.play.priority.title: Call priority
satori.help.play.priority.body: Ron takes priority over chi, pon and kan; pon and kan take priority over chi. This table allows multiple ron: the discarder pays each winner the value of their hand.
satori.help.play.pass.title: Passing a call
satori.help.play.pass.body: Pass to decline chi, pon or kan and let play continue. Passing an available ron causes furiten. A win needs a complete shape, a yaku and compliance with furiten restrictions.
satori.help.yaku.read.title: Yaku and han
satori.help.yaku.read.body: Headings show han; each entry states closed/open-hand and timing conditions. A green outline marks the winning tile. Sideways tiles mark open calls; concealed kans have backs at both ends. Examples may combine other yaku. Local yaku are not used.
satori.help.yaku.riichi.title: Riichi · 1 han · closed
satori.help.yaku.riichi.body: Declare a ready closed hand, pay 1,000 points and make the declaration discard. Afterward you normally discard each drawn tile. See Riichi / waits.
satori.help.yaku.tsumo.title: Menzen Tsumo · 1 han · closed
satori.help.yaku.tsumo.body: Complete a closed hand on your own draw. An open hand may still win by tsumo, but the draw itself no longer supplies this yaku.
satori.help.yaku.tanyao.title: All Simples / Tanyao · 1 han
satori.help.yaku.tanyao.body: Every tile is a number from 2 to 8: no terminals or honors. Open All Simples is allowed at this table.
satori.help.yaku.yakuhai.title: Value Tiles / Yakuhai · 1 han per value
satori.help.yaku.yakuhai.body: A triplet or kan of white, green or red dragons, your seat wind or the round wind. East as dealer in the East round is worth two han. Other wind triplets are not yaku.
satori.help.yaku.pinfu.title: Pinfu · 1 han · closed
satori.help.yaku.pinfu.body: Four sequences, a pair with no dragon, seat-wind or round-wind value, and a two-sided wait. Waiting on 2 or 5 with 34 qualifies; 12, 35 and a single-tile pair wait do not.
satori.help.yaku.iipeikou.title: Pure Double Sequence / Iipeikou · 1 han · closed
satori.help.yaku.iipeikou.body: Two identical sequences in one suit, such as two groups of 234 characters.
satori.help.yaku.ippatsu.title: Ippatsu · 1 han · after riichi
satori.help.yaku.ippatsu.body: Win after declaring riichi and before discarding after your next draw, including that draw. Any chi, pon or kan interrupts it, including your own concealed kan.
satori.help.yaku.haitei.title: Last Draw / Haitei · 1 han
satori.help.yaku.haitei.body: Win on the last normal draw from the live wall. A kan replacement draw is not Haitei.
satori.help.yaku.houtei.title: Last Discard / Houtei · 1 han
satori.help.yaku.houtei.body: Win by ron on the final discard after the live wall is exhausted.
satori.help.yaku.rinshan.title: Kan Replacement / Rinshan · 1 han
satori.help.yaku.rinshan.body: Win by tsumo on the replacement tile drawn after declaring a kan.
satori.help.yaku.chankan.title: Robbing a Kan / Chankan · 1 han
satori.help.yaku.chankan.body: Ron on the fourth tile used to extend an exposed pon into an added kan. An open kan cannot be robbed. Concealed kans cannot be robbed at this table.
satori.help.yaku.double_riichi.title: Double Riichi · 2 han · closed
satori.help.yaku.double_riichi.body: Declare riichi on your first discard, before any chi, pon or kan. This replaces ordinary Riichi rather than adding to it.
satori.help.yaku.chiitoitsu.title: Seven Pairs / Chiitoitsu · 2 han · closed
satori.help.yaku.chiitoitsu.body: Seven different pairs. Four identical tiles do not count as two pairs. This shape has a fixed 25 fu and is not also scored as four groups and a pair.
satori.help.yaku.toitoi.title: All Triplets / Toitoi · 2 han
satori.help.yaku.toitoi.body: Four triplets or kans and a pair, with no sequences.
satori.help.yaku.sanankou.title: Three Concealed Triplets / Sanankou · 2 han
satori.help.yaku.sanankou.body: Three concealed triplets or concealed kans. A triplet completed by ron is exposed for this purpose; winning on a pair or sequence does not expose your other triplets.
satori.help.yaku.sankantsu.title: Three Kans / Sankantsu · 2 han
satori.help.yaku.sankantsu.body: Three declared kans, open or concealed.
satori.help.yaku.sanshoku_doukou.title: Triple Triplets / Sanshoku Doukou · 2 han
satori.help.yaku.sanshoku_doukou.body: Matching-number triplets or kans in all three suits, such as three sevens in each suit.
satori.help.yaku.shousangen.title: Little Three Dragons / Shousangen · 2 han
satori.help.yaku.shousangen.body: Two dragon triplets or kans and a pair of the third dragon. The two dragon Value Tile yaku are also counted.
satori.help.yaku.honroutou.title: All Terminals and Honors / Honroutou · 2 han
satori.help.yaku.honroutou.body: Only terminals and honors. Usually combines with All Triplets, but a Seven Pairs shape can also qualify. No sequences.
satori.help.yaku.sanshoku_doujun.title: Mixed Triple Sequence / Sanshoku Doujun · 2 closed, 1 open
satori.help.yaku.sanshoku_doujun.body: The same numbered sequence in all three suits, such as 234 characters, 234 dots and 234 bamboo.
satori.help.yaku.ittsuu.title: Pure Straight / Ittsuu · 2 closed, 1 open
satori.help.yaku.ittsuu.body: Sequences 123, 456 and 789 in one suit. Merely holding all numbers 1–9 is not enough; they must form those groups.
satori.help.yaku.chanta.title: Mixed Outside Hand / Chanta · 2 closed, 1 open
satori.help.yaku.chanta.body: Every group and the pair contains a terminal or honor, with at least one sequence and at least one honor. With no honors, use Junchan instead.
satori.help.yaku.ryanpeikou.title: Twice Pure Double Sequence / Ryanpeikou · 3 han · closed
satori.help.yaku.ryanpeikou.body: Four sequences form two pairs of identical sequences, plus the pair. Replaces Iipeikou and does not combine with Seven Pairs.
satori.help.yaku.junchan.title: Pure Outside Hand / Junchan · 3 closed, 2 open
satori.help.yaku.junchan.body: Every group and the pair contains a 1 or 9, with no honors and at least one sequence. Does not also score Chanta.
satori.help.yaku.honitsu.title: Half Flush / Honitsu · 3 closed, 2 open
satori.help.yaku.honitsu.body: One numbered suit and honors, with both present. With no honors, use Full Flush instead.
satori.help.yaku.chinitsu.title: Full Flush / Chinitsu · 6 closed, 5 open
satori.help.yaku.chinitsu.body: Only one numbered suit, with no honors. Does not also score Half Flush.
satori.help.yaku.kokushi.title: Thirteen Orphans / Kokushi · yakuman · closed
satori.help.yaku.kokushi.body: One of each of the 13 terminals and honors, plus a duplicate of one of them. The thirteen-sided wait is also a single yakuman.
satori.help.yaku.suuankou.title: Four Concealed Triplets / Suuankou · yakuman · closed
satori.help.yaku.suuankou.body: Four concealed triplets or kans and a pair. A two-pair wait needs tsumo; ron is allowed on a single-tile pair wait. Both versions are single yakuman.
satori.help.yaku.daisangen.title: Big Three Dragons / Daisangen · yakuman
satori.help.yaku.daisangen.body: Triplets or kans of all three dragons, another group and a pair.
satori.help.yaku.shousuushi.title: Little Four Winds / Shousuushi · yakuman
satori.help.yaku.shousuushi.body: Three wind triplets or kans and a pair of the fourth wind.
satori.help.yaku.daisuushi.title: Big Four Winds / Daisuushi · yakuman
satori.help.yaku.daisuushi.body: Triplets or kans of all four winds and a pair. A single yakuman at this table.
satori.help.yaku.tsuuiisou.title: All Honors / Tsuuiisou · yakuman
satori.help.yaku.tsuuiisou.body: Only honor tiles, using either four groups and a pair or Seven Pairs.
satori.help.yaku.chinroutou.title: All Terminals / Chinroutou · yakuman
satori.help.yaku.chinroutou.body: Only suited 1s and 9s, with no honors: four triplets or kans and a pair.
satori.help.yaku.ryuuiisou.title: All Green / Ryuuiisou · yakuman
satori.help.yaku.ryuuiisou.body: Use only bamboo 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 and green dragons. Green dragons are optional; 234 bamboo sequences are allowed.
satori.help.yaku.chuuren.title: Nine Gates / Chuuren · yakuman · closed
satori.help.yaku.chuuren.body: 1112345678999 in one suit, plus any tile in that suit. No kans. The pure nine-sided wait is also a single yakuman.
satori.help.yaku.suukantsu.title: Four Kans / Suukantsu · yakuman
satori.help.yaku.suukantsu.body: One player declares all four kans and completes the pair. Open and concealed kans both count.
satori.help.yaku.tenhou.title: Heavenly Hand / Tenhou · yakuman · dealer
satori.help.yaku.tenhou.body: The dealer wins immediately with the initial hand, before discarding or declaring a kan. Scored as one yakuman on its own at this table.
satori.help.yaku.chiihou.title: Earthly Hand / Chiihou · yakuman · non-dealer
satori.help.yaku.chiihou.body: A non-dealer wins on the first draw, before any chi, pon or kan. Scored as one yakuman on its own at this table.
satori.help.yaku.counted.title: Counted yakuman and multiple yakuman
satori.help.yaku.counted.body: Ordinary yaku plus dora reaching 13 han score as a counted yakuman. Natural yakuman do not add ordinary yaku or dora. Compatible natural yakuman can stack, such as All Honors with Big Three Dragons.
satori.help.riichi.declare.title: Riichi conditions
satori.help.riichi.declare.body: You must be closed, ready after discarding, have at least 1,000 points, and have at least four live-wall tiles remaining. Choose riichi and a legal declaration discard. The 1,000-point deposit is accepted if that discard is not won on.
satori.help.riichi.locked.title: Riichi locks the hand
satori.help.riichi.locked.body: Normally discard each new draw, or win by tsumo or ron. You cannot chi, pon or add a kan. Only concealed kans meeting the post-riichi restrictions are offered. Riichi cannot be withdrawn.
satori.help.riichi.ippatsu.title: Ippatsu, ura dora and deposits
satori.help.riichi.ippatsu.body: Riichi enables Ippatsu and reveals ura dora if you win. Ura dora may add no value. Accepted riichi deposits stay in the center until a winner takes them; a drawn hand carries them forward.
satori.help.riichi.discard_furiten.title: Discard furiten checks every wait
satori.help.riichi.discard_furiten.body: If any tile completing your current shape is in your discard history, ron is blocked on all waits, even when that discarded tile gives no yaku. Discards later called by others still count. Changing the hand can clear this if none of the new waits match your history.
satori.help.riichi.temporary.title: Temporary furiten after passing ron
satori.help.riichi.temporary.body: Without riichi, letting a tile completing your shape pass causes temporary furiten, even if that tile gives no yaku. Ron is blocked until your next draw and discard; tsumo remains possible. A discard after your own chi or pon also rechecks the waits.
satori.help.riichi.riichi_furiten.title: Passing ron after riichi
satori.help.riichi.riichi_furiten.body: After riichi, passing a legal ron blocks ron for the rest of the hand, on every wait. Tsumo remains possible. Declaring riichi while already in discard furiten does not clear it.
satori.help.riichi.waits.title: Common wait shapes
satori.help.riichi.waits.body: 34 waiting on 2/5 is two-sided; 35 waiting on 4 is closed; 12 waiting on 3 is edge. Two pairs waiting to complete a triplet is a double-pair wait; one tile waiting to form the pair is a single-pair wait. Wait shape affects Pinfu, fu and Suuankou.
satori.help.scoring.han_fu.title: Han and fu
satori.help.scoring.han_fu.body: First establish a yaku, then total han including dora. Fu comes from the base, groups, value pairs, waits and win method, normally rounded up to ten. Seven Pairs is 25 fu; Pinfu tsumo is 20 fu. Equal han can still produce different scores.
satori.help.scoring.payments.title: Normally: discarder pays ron, others pay tsumo
satori.help.scoring.payments.body: The discarder pays ron. On a non-dealer tsumo the dealer pays more; on dealer tsumo all three pay equally. Example: non-dealer 30 fu, 1 han is 1,000 ron or 500 from dealer and 300 from each other player. Each honba normally adds 300 total: 300 on ron or 100 each on tsumo.
satori.help.scoring.limits.title: Score limits
satori.help.scoring.limits.body: Non-dealer ron: mangan 8,000; haneman 12,000; baiman 16,000; sanbaiman 24,000; yakuman 32,000. Dealer scores are 1.5 times these. Limits start at 5, 6–7, 8–10, 11–12 and 13+ han respectively. 4 han 40 fu or 3 han 70 fu reaches mangan; 4 han 30 fu remains 7,700.
satori.help.scoring.dora_cycle.title: Reading dora indicators
satori.help.scoring.dora_cycle.body: The indicated tile is followed by the dora: numbers cycle 1–9; winds East → South → West → North; dragons white → green → red. A 3-character indicator means 4 characters is dora. Each copy adds one han; repeated indicators stack. Red fives add another han; ura dora counts only for riichi winners.
satori.help.scoring.draw.title: Exhaustive draw
satori.help.scoring.draw.body: If nobody wins, check tenpai. When some but not all players are ready, 3,000 points move from not-ready to ready players: one ready gets 3,000, two get 1,500 each, three get 1,000 each. All-ready and none-ready have no payment. Tenpai for this check does not require a yaku. A ready dealer repeats.
satori.help.scoring.nagashi.title: Nagashi Mangan
satori.help.scoring.nagashi.body: At an exhaustive draw, every one of your discards must be a terminal or honor and none may have been called. You receive a mangan tsumo payment without needing tenpai. Your own earlier calls are allowed here. Noten payments are not applied when Nagashi Mangan occurs.
satori.help.scoring.abort.title: Abortive draws
satori.help.scoring.abort.body: Before calls interrupt the first turn, nine or more different terminals and honors allow Nine Terminals. Four identical first wind discards with no intervening calls also end the hand, as do four riichi or four kans split between players. Four kans by one player continue. No noten payments apply.
satori.help.scoring.match.title: Hands, East-only and half games
satori.help.scoring.match.body: Four players start with 25,000 each. The dealer repeats after winning, a ready exhaustive draw, or an abortive draw. Otherwise dealership rotates. East-only games cover the East round; half games cover East and South. Repeats add hands, and unmet end conditions can extend play. Negative points end the match; zero does not. Final scores determine places.
satori.help.scoring.pao.title: Responsibility payments / Pao
satori.help.scoring.pao.body: If a player has two exposed dragon triplets or three exposed wind triplets, supplying the final call for Big Three Dragons or Big Four Winds creates responsibility. You pay alone if they tsumo. If a third player deals in, you and the discarder each pay half of the winning hand's value.

satori.help.sichuan.basics.win.title: Clear the void suit to win
satori.help.sichuan.basics.win.body: After clearing your declared void suit, complete four sets and a pair, or seven pairs. A plain hand can win; no riichi yaku is required.
satori.help.sichuan.basics.void.title: Declare a void suit
satori.help.sichuan.basics.void.body: After exchanging, declare Characters, Circles or Bamboo void. Void tiles move to the right with a corner mark. You may discard another suit first. Void tiles cannot be used for Pung or Kong, and any remaining void tile prevents a win.
satori.help.sichuan.basics.battle.title: The round continues after a win
satori.help.sichuan.basics.battle.body: Winners stop playing while the others continue. Only the winning tile is public until the end of the hand. The hand ends after three players win or the wall runs out. Multiple players may win on one discard.
satori.help.sichuan.basics.shape.title: Sets and pairs
satori.help.sichuan.basics.shape.body: Three consecutive tiles in one suit form a sequence, three identical tiles a triplet, and two identical tiles a pair. Sequences count in your hand, but chi is unavailable. Pon and kan form exposed sets.
satori.help.sichuan.basics.scope.title: Rules used at this table
satori.help.sichuan.basics.scope.body: Four-player Blood Battle with Exchange Three, using 108 suited tiles. No Honors, red fives or Dora. New tables cap at 4 Fan, add 1 Fan for self-draw and settle Kongs immediately. Existing games retain their agreed settings.
satori.help.sichuan.basics.example.title: A complete winning hand
satori.help.sichuan.basics.example.body: Four sets and a pair with no bamboo, the declared void suit. This hand can win on a discard. A self-draw adds one fan. The green border marks the winning tile.
satori.help.sichuan.play.tiles.title: Tiles and dealing
satori.help.sichuan.play.tiles.body: Characters, Circles and Bamboo each have nine ranks and four copies: 108 tiles. Each player starts with 13 tiles. Exchange three, declare a void suit, then the dealer draws first. The final bottom tile is left unused.
satori.help.sichuan.play.void.title: Void-suit controls
satori.help.sichuan.play.void.body: Drawing starts after all players declare a void suit. Its tiles stay in the hand, move to the right and receive a corner mark. New tables allow discarding another suit first; clear the void suit before winning.
satori.help.sichuan.play.turn.title: Draw and discard
satori.help.sichuan.play.turn.body: Draw and discard on your turn. New tables allow discarding another suit first; clear your void suit before winning. Legal wins and Kongs appear as buttons. Discard after a Pung without drawing. Skip seats that have already won. Clicking a held tile is a hand discard; clicking the drawn tile is a draw discard, even for identical faces. Ready-hand hints show waits; hover a legal discard to inspect its resulting waits.
satori.help.sichuan.play.calls.title: Pon and discard wins
satori.help.sichuan.play.calls.body: Call pon to combine a discard with two identical tiles. Win on a discard when your hand is complete and clear of its void suit. Chi is unavailable.
satori.help.sichuan.play.kans.title: Three kinds of kan
satori.help.sichuan.play.kans.body: A concealed kan uses four identical tiles in hand. An open kan combines a discard with three held tiles. An added kan adds the fourth tile to an existing pon. A kan pays immediately and receives a replacement draw.
satori.help.sichuan.play.pass.title: Passing a response
satori.help.sichuan.play.pass.body: Pass declines the current pon, kan or win opportunity. This variant has no riichi furiten. New legal opportunities are evaluated by the server when they occur.
satori.help.sichuan.play.won.title: After winning
satori.help.sichuan.play.won.body: Win payments update immediately while the others continue. Only the winning tile is public until the hand ends. You retain your own view; spectators follow the table policy. Winners stop drawing, discarding and paying later wins or Kongs.
satori.help.sichuan.yaku.read.title: Adding fan
satori.help.sichuan.yaku.read.body: Add applicable patterns and bonuses, up to four Fan on new tables. Four identical tiles in seven pairs count as a dragon and do not also count as a root. Examples illustrate the named condition; the total also depends on other patterns and win timing.
satori.help.sichuan.yaku.pinghu.title: Plain hand · 0 fan
satori.help.sichuan.yaku.pinghu.body: Four sets and a pair with no additional pattern. Clear the void suit to win. A zero-fan discard win pays one point.
satori.help.sichuan.yaku.duidui.title: All triplets · 1 fan
satori.help.sichuan.yaku.duidui.body: Four triplets or kans and a pair. Exposed pon and kan are allowed; sequences do not qualify.
satori.help.sichuan.yaku.qingyise.title: Full flush · 2 fan
satori.help.sichuan.yaku.qingyise.body: All concealed tiles and melds belong to one suit. This can combine with other eligible patterns.
satori.help.sichuan.yaku.qidui.title: Seven pairs · 2 fan
satori.help.sichuan.yaku.qidui.body: A concealed hand of seven pairs. Four identical tiles can form two pairs and qualify as a dragon.
satori.help.sichuan.yaku.longqidui.title: Dragon seven pairs · +1 per dragon
satori.help.sichuan.yaku.longqidui.body: In seven pairs, each group of four identical tiles adds one fan to the base two fan. Two such groups make double dragon seven pairs. The same group is not counted again as a root.
satori.help.sichuan.yaku.quandaiyao.body: Every set and the pair contain a one or nine. Sequences must be 123 or 789; triplets, kans and the pair must be ones or nines.
satori.help.sichuan.yaku.jiangdui.title: All 2/5/8 triplets · +2 fan
satori.help.sichuan.yaku.jiangdui.body: An all-triplet hand using only twos, fives and eights adds two fan to the one fan for all triplets.
satori.help.sichuan.yaku.jingou.title: Single-pair wait · 1 fan
satori.help.sichuan.yaku.jingou.body: With four completed melds, hold one tile and wait for its pair. A concealed kan also counts toward the four completed melds.
satori.help.sichuan.yaku.gen.title: Root · +1 fan each
satori.help.sichuan.yaku.gen.body: In a standard hand, four copies of one tile across the hand and melds form a root, even without a kan. Each root adds one fan. Seven-pairs quads use dragon scoring instead.
satori.help.sichuan.yaku.zimo.title: Self-draw · +1 fan
satori.help.sichuan.yaku.zimo.body: Drawing your own winning tile adds one fan. Only the other players who have not yet won pay the final value.
satori.help.sichuan.yaku.rinshan.title: Kan replacement win · +1 fan
satori.help.sichuan.yaku.rinshan.body: Winning on the replacement draw after a kan adds one fan, in addition to the self-draw bonus.
satori.help.sichuan.yaku.chankan.title: Robbing an added kan · +1 fan
satori.help.sichuan.yaku.chankan.body: Win on a tile being added to another player’s pon. Add one fan, paid by that player. The added kan is cancelled.
satori.help.sichuan.yaku.haidi.title: Last live tile · +1 fan
satori.help.sichuan.yaku.haidi.body: Add one fan for a win on the last live draw or its discard. The unused bottom tile is not part of the live wall.
satori.help.sichuan.yaku.tiandi.title: Heavenly and earthly wins · table cap
satori.help.sichuan.yaku.tiandi.body: The dealer winning on the opening draw is Heavenly Hand. A non-dealer winning on the first uninterrupted draw is Earthly Hand. Both pay the table cap, which is 4 Fan on new tables.
satori.help.sichuan.battle.choose.title: One fixed void suit per round
satori.help.sichuan.battle.choose.body: Choose a void suit anew each round. Your choice is fixed for that round. Individual declarations remain private until all players have responded.
satori.help.sichuan.battle.restrict.body: On new tables, discard every void-suit tile before using other suits. Pung, Kong and winning are unavailable until the suit is clear. Declaring a void does not remove its tiles; newly drawn void tiles must also be discarded first.
satori.help.sichuan.battle.priority.body: All legal winners on the same discard are settled; pon and kan responses are then ignored. Without a win, meld responses follow seat order after the discarder.
satori.help.sichuan.battle.continue.body: After winning, keep your score and show only the winning tile. Concealed tiles remain private until the hand ends. Turns continue after the discarder, skipping winners. The next hand starts with a new deal, exchange and void declaration.
satori.help.sichuan.battle.end.title: Round ending
satori.help.sichuan.battle.end.body: The third winner ends the round. If the live wall runs out first, kan refunds and void-suit and not-ready penalties settle before round confirmation.
satori.help.sichuan.scoring.units.title: Base 1, capped at 4 Fan
satori.help.sichuan.scoring.units.body: New tables pay 1 × 2 to the Fan power, capped at 4 Fan: 0 Fan = 1, 1 = 2, 2 = 4, 3 = 8, and 4 or more = 16. The self-draw Fan is included before applying the cap.
satori.help.sichuan.scoring.payments.tit: Discarder pays, live players pay self-draws
satori.help.sichuan.scoring.payments.bod: The discarder pays each winner separately. For a self-draw, every other player still in the round pays one share. Earlier winners pay nothing.
satori.help.sichuan.scoring.kan.title: Immediate kan payments
satori.help.sichuan.scoring.kan.body: Open kan: the discarder pays two points. Added kan: each other live player pays one. Concealed kan: each other live player pays two. A robbed added kan receives no kan payment.
satori.help.sichuan.scoring.tax.title: Kan refunds on an exhausted wall
satori.help.sichuan.scoring.tax.body: At an exhaustive draw, non-winning, non-ready players refund every Kong payment they received to its original payer. Forbidden-suit violators also refund. Winners and ready players retain their Kong income. Refunds and both draw penalties appear separately.
satori.help.sichuan.scoring.pig.title: Forbidden-suit penalty: 16 per player
satori.help.sichuan.scoring.pig.body: At an exhaustive draw, a player still holding their void suit pays the table cap to each player without that violation, including earlier winners. New tables pay 16 each. Violators do not pay each other and do not also pay the not-ready penalty.
satori.help.sichuan.scoring.ready.title: Not-ready payments
satori.help.sichuan.scoring.ready.body: A non-winning player who has cleared the void suit but is not ready pays each remaining ready player their maximum legal hand value, capped by the table. Self-draw and timing bonuses do not apply. Earlier winners are excluded. The summary lists each payer, recipient and amount.
satori.help.sichuan.scoring.match.title: 4, 8 or 16 rounds
satori.help.sichuan.scoring.match.body: Choose the round count in the lobby. Confirm after each round. The dealer rotates by seat without repeats. Start at zero points and rank by the match total; scores may be negative.

satori.help.sichuan.example.longqidui: Void bamboo; four ones form two pairs and one dragon.
satori.help.sichuan.example.quandaiyao: Void bamboo; each set and the pair contain a terminal.
satori.help.sichuan.example.jiangdui: Void bamboo; all triplets and the pair use twos, fives or eights.
satori.help.sichuan.example.jingou: Void bamboo; four exposed pons with a five-character pair wait.
satori.help.sichuan.example.gen: Void bamboo; the triplet and 123 sequence use all four ones.
satori.help.sichuan.example.zimo: Void bamboo; draw the winning five yourself.
satori.help.sichuan.example.rinshan: Void bamboo; draw the winning five after a concealed kan of ones.
satori.help.sichuan.example.chankan: Void bamboo; win on the five being added to another player’s pon.
satori.help.sichuan.example.haidi: Void bamboo; the last live draw is the winning five.
satori.help.sichuan.example.tiandi: Void bamboo; this first-turn self-draw requires the matching discard and call history.
satori.table.exchange_select: Choose three tiles of one suit (%s/3)
satori.help.sichuan.basics.exchange.titl: Exchange three before choosing a void suit
satori.help.sichuan.basics.exchange.body: Choose three tiles of one suit. After all four players confirm, exchange simultaneously in one randomly selected direction: next, opposite or previous seat. Choose your void suit after receiving the tiles.
satori.help.sichuan.play.exchange.title: Selecting three tiles
satori.help.sichuan.play.exchange.body: Click three tiles in your own hand. Gold outlines mark your selection; click again to cancel. Confirm is enabled for a legal selection. All players exchange together, and other participants cannot see your sent or received tiles.
